reading.body:
Bolt.new routes user requests to different AI models based on task complexity and cost, removing the need for users to manually select between AI agents or platforms.

The product sits at the intersection of developer tools and AI orchestration. By automatically matching tasks to appropriate models, it abstracts away model selection from the user. This approach addresses a real friction point: as the AI landscape fragments across specialized models optimized for different workloads, end users gain no benefit from knowing which model is best for their task.

For AI infrastructure, this pattern matters because it shifts model selection from human choice to algorithmic routing. If millions of users generate code through Bolt.new, the company becomes an intermediary that shapes demand across AI providers. The tool's cost-optimization logic means it has an incentive to route tasks toward cheaper models when quality allows, directly affecting which models see actual inference workload.

The data does not cover Bolt.new's actual routing decisions, which models it uses, infrastructure costs, or compute consumption. It does not specify whether the product is constrained by API rate limits from model providers or by its own serving capacity. Those details would matter far more than the feature description for understanding whether Bolt.new functions as a load-balancer or a demand aggregator in the broader AI ecosystem.

profile_text.body:
StackBlitz is the company behind Bolt.new, an AI-powered builder that the site describes as enabling users to create websites, applications, and prototypes using natural language input. The site positions Bolt.new as a tool for building and scaling web projects, and states that it has attracted millions of users.

Bolt.new is categorized as a coding and developer tool focused on app generation. According to the site, the product automatically routes tasks to an appropriate AI model, balancing quality and cost, with the stated aim of removing the need for users to manage multiple platforms or select between different AI agents themselves.

The held facts confirm that StackBlitz has a tracked presence on theworldofai.org with Bolt.new listed as its primary product. No litigation, MCP servers, SEC filings, or patent records are noted in the available data.
